items.excerpt: Nine stories, U.S. first: a nationwide FAA ground stop, a tanker crash into a cruise boat in New Orleans, a Supreme Court asylum case, Starship's latest test, a Medicaid work rule delay and a planned Trump-Xi-Putin meeting; then Iran and Bahrain, a deadly crash in India and a drone attack in Russia. ... ### FAA ground stop halts flights nationwide The FAA halted all departures across the U.S. for more than four hours Friday after a communications failure at air traffic control centers. Thousands of flights were canceled, and delays continued into Saturday. ### Tanker hits docked cruise boat in New Orleans; all survive A tanker that apparently lost steering slammed into a docked river cruise boat on the Mississippi River in New Orleans, tipping it onto its side. Everyone aboard survived; 32 people were taken to hospitals with non-critical injuries. ### Supreme Court to weigh Trump's asylum ban The Supreme Court agreed to decide whether President Trump's order suspending asylum access at the southern border is legal. Lower courts found the policy illegal; arguments are expected in spring 2027. ### Starship reaches orbit as booster explodes SpaceX's Starship reached orbit on its 15th test flight and deployed 26 Starlink satellites, but the Super Heavy booster exploded over the Gulf of Mexico after a planned launch-tower catch was called off. ### States get six more months on Medicaid work rule The Trump administration will let states take an optional six-month grace period, through June 30, 2027, before removing people from Medicaid for not meeting the new work requirement. ### Trump, Xi and Putin to meet in Shenzhen The White House says President Trump will hold an unprecedented three-way meeting with China's Xi Jinping and Russia's Vladimir Putin on Nov. 19 in Shenzhen, on the sidelines of the APEC summit. ### Iran claims strike on U.S. radar in Bahrain; U.S. denies Iran's Revolutionary Guards said they destroyed a U.S. early-warning radar in Bahrain in retaliation for a strike on a telecom tower in Sirik, Iran. U.S. Central Command said it shot down two Iranian drones and there was no damage. ### Bus-truck crash kills 26 in India's Assam A minibus collided head-on with a container truck on a highway near Kaziranga National Park in India's Assam state, killing 26 people, many of them college students, officials said. ### Ukrainian drones kill 4 in Volgograd A Ukrainian drone attack killed four workers and injured two in an industrial zone in the southern Russian city of Volgograd, the regional governor said. Ukraine said it hit the city's oil refinery.

items.title: Wholesale food prices are on the rise
items.excerpt: Food prices are rising sharply even before they reach supermarket shelves. Why it matters: Americans are already paying more for groceries. New inflation data this week suggests that the pressure is not letting up. - Wholesale fresh and dry vegetable prices surged 27% last month, adding to a 31% price jump the previous month. - These are the prices paid by food distributors, grocery chains and other businesses to farmers and other producers for eventual sale to consumers. - Wholesale food prices overall are up 1.7% from a year earlier, ending a three-month streak of annual price declines. Zoom in: Unusually warm weather, crop disease and insect infestations have reduced lettuce and other leafy green harvests in California. - The Iran war, meanwhile, has driven up the cost of fertilizer and fuel, making it more expensive to grow and transport food. - A regional grocery chain recently told Federal Reserve officials that it now costs more to transport a head of lettuce from California than to buy the lettuce itself, citing high diesel fuel prices. - Truck freight costs are up almost 25% over the past year, the largest annual increase since 2022 and on par with the surge seen during the pandemic-era inflation shock. The big picture: It's unclear how much of the surge in producer prices will be passed along to consumers. But steeper price increases were already showing up at supermarket checkout counters last month. - Grocery prices rose 0.4%, the biggest monthly increase in 6 months, driven by higher prices for meat, dairy products and snack foods. - Fresh vegetable prices climbed 2%, including a nearly 8% jump in lettuce prices.

items.title: Bessent, Fed official divided on role of energy shock in inflation - Gulf Times
items.excerpt: Reuters/ Washington Published on November 14, 2026 | 12:00 AM ... US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said on Friday that the Federal Reserve should not hike rates because of inflation driven by an "energy supply shock" tied to the Iran war, comments made to CNBC and promptly contradicted on the network by Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee, who said price pressures were building far beyond what could be explained by high oil prices. "I think the Fed should understand that this is an energy supply shock," while the underlying US economy is very strong, Bessent said in an interview on CNBC. "So I think that to hike too much into an energy supply shock when it's coming down, these are very noisy numbers...You know, the Fed's supposed to look into the future, not look in the rearview mirror." Shortly afterwards, the network hosted Goolsbee, a regular guest on CNBC's morning Squawk Box show, who said that inflation was not just due to energy, but had spread to the service sector and areas like medical care that are not usually responsive to the price of oil, and was also elevated through strong demand tied to the AI data centre buildout. "I respect the secretary and I am trying to figure out the same thing he is trying to figure out, which is how persistent is this inflation? The tariff inflation and oil price shock were supposed to have gone away by now and it hasn't," Goolsbee said. "One puzzle is why have those supply shocks been as persistent as they have been. A second thing is if demand is overheating and that is contributing to inflation, that is more worrisome... Services inflation, which is probably not coming from tariffs or oil, is one of the more troubling aspects of the inflation reports we have been getting." While not committing to a rate hike, he said the Fed "has definitely got work to do to continue to reestablish its credibility." ... Fed policymakers were open to the possibility they could "look through" supply-driven inflation at the start of the US war with Iran. But as inflation remained lodged above the Fed's target, concern about it grew, as did support for rate hikes. Research meanwhile opened a different window on the relationship between oil prices and US inflation. Because the US is an energy exporter, higher global oil prices can filter through to the economy in the form of higher corporate profits and wages, providing a source of inflation beyond supply issues that can't be easily ignored by the central bank. Recent stronger-than-expected jobs and inflation reports have further bolstered the case for more Federal Reserve interest rate hikes, and even prompted some officials to discuss the need for a larger-than-typical half-percentage-point increase at the central bank's coming December 8-9 meeting. "We have had signs of trouble now for several months in a row if you look at how broad-based the inflation is," Goolsbee said. "In categories that are not driven by oil prices and not driven by tariffs, you are still seeing stalled progress and in some cases going the wrong way ... That is not going away no matter what happens to the price of oil." "Are we on a path back to 2%? My feeling right now is we are not and we've got to deal with that," Goolsbee said. "Conventional wisdom says do everything you can to prevent demand overheating," Goolsbee said, with coming data on inflation the key to whether the Fed needs a faster pace of rate increases.

items.title: Goldman blames tariffs, Iran shock for inflation gap - MacroHerald
items.excerpt: Goldman Sachs economists have published a chart attributing almost all of the recent US inflation overshoot to tariffs and the energy shock tied to Iran, arguing that once these temporary drivers are stripped out, underlying inflation sits near the Federal Reserve’s target. The note followed Tuesday’s release of October CPI data. ... ## Temporary drivers, lasting policy shift US headline personal consumption expenditures inflation ran at 3.6 percent year on year in September, with core PCE at 3.1 percent. Gasoline and other energy goods prices jumped 9.2 percent month on month in September, a move Goldman links to the Iran energy shock. The bank expects headline PCE to peak just shy of 3.9 percent and core PCE to peak near 3.3 percent, before easing back. Strip out the temporary drivers, and Goldman puts headline PCE at 2.2 percent and core PCE at 2.4 percent. The bank estimates the energy and Iran effect adds about 1.5 percentage points to headline PCE at its peak, with tariffs contributing a further 0.3 to 0.4 percentage points. Core services inflation excluding housing ran at 3.6 percent year on year in September. Goldman expects tariff effects to have largely faded by mid-2027 and the energy effect to fade through late 2027, with headline PCE settling near 2.1 percent by the end of that year. ... Goldman has added a rate hike to its Fed forecast, now expecting 25 basis points of tightening in December and a further 25 basis points in March. The bank’s first projected rate cut has been pushed back to December 2027.

items.title: Fed's Jefferson Says Inflation Path Will Carry More Weight in Policy | EconoTimes
items.excerpt: Federal Reserve Vice Chair Philip N. Jefferson said inflation’s direction should weigh more heavily in future U.S. rate decisions, leaving the timing and size of any policy change open. Speaking at the University of California, San Diego Economic Roundtable on Nov. 13, Jefferson described price pressures as persistent. “I see the trajectory of inflation as providing the more important signal,” he said. Any policy adjustment, he added, should account for data trends, the outlook and the balance of risks. He said his remarks represented his own views, not necessarily those of his Federal Reserve Board colleagues or the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC). The FOMC kept its federal funds target range at 3.75% to 4.00% at its Oct. 27-28 meeting, voting 10-2. FOMC members Lisa D. Cook and Beth M. Hammack dissented in favor of a 25-basis-point increase. The latest personal consumption expenditures (PCE) data showed prices rose 3.6% in the 12 months through September, while the core index, which excludes food and energy, increased 3.1%, the Bureau of Economic Analysis (BEA) reported. October’s Consumer Price Index (CPI) rose 0.4% from September on a seasonally adjusted basis, and core CPI gained 0.3%, the Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) said. The BLS did not publish most year-over-year October comparisons because October 2025 survey data were unavailable after a lapse in appropriations. The BEA’s advance estimate showed real gross domestic product grew at a 3.4% annual rate in the third quarter of 2026. Separately, the BLS reported that the unemployment rate was 4.1% in October 2026 and payroll employment increased by 165,000.

items.title: Goolsbee Says Broader Inflation Could Prompt a Tougher Fed Response | EconoTimes
items.excerpt: Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee said Friday that worsening inflation data could require a more forceful Federal Reserve response, as U.S. policymakers assess whether price pressures are spreading beyond energy. Goolsbee made the remarks in a Nov. 13 interview on CNBC’s Squawk Box, which the Chicago Fed lists on its media appearances page. He said inflation had reached categories not driven by energy. His response was conditional on incoming data, and he did not commit to a rate increase. The U.S. Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) reported that the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (CPI) rose 0.4% in October, after a 0.6% increase in September. Core CPI, which excludes food and energy, rose 0.3% month over month in August, September and October. Because the BLS did not collect October 2025 data during the lapse in appropriations, it could not publish 12-month changes for most CPI series. EconoTimes previously covered October’s CPI report and Goolsbee’s comments on services inflation. Producer prices also rose. The BLS said its final-demand Producer Price Index (PPI) increased 0.3% in October and 6.5% over the 12 months through October. That annual increase was the largest since November 2022, when it was 7.4%. The CPI figures provide monthly comparisons, while the missing October 2025 data prevent most annual comparisons in the latest consumer-price release. The Fed’s longer-run inflation goal is 2%, measured using annual changes in the personal consumption expenditures (PCE) price index. On Oct. 28, the Federal Open Market Committee (FOMC) kept its federal funds target range at 3.75% to 4.00%; two members preferred a quarter-point increase.

items.excerpt: ELVING: It has a lot of appeal, especially to younger voters, first-time voters, independents - the people who fueled this extraordinary Democratic surge, especially in the Senate races that Democrats won when nobody thought they were even close. And yes, the voters want an end to corruption and a rigged economy. But when Van Hollen says he wants to organize the Senate in a different way to achieve those ends, does he just mean a new leader, someone other than the longtime leader Chuck Schumer? What else do we know will change? And how do we know it will be better? Schumer says he has the vote commitments for most of the Senate Democrats already. He needs 29. Some of his allies are saying he'll have 40 votes or more. But Van Hollen still has time to make his case, and in the end, the vote is cast by secret ballot. And I've seen leadership elections in the past where someone claimed to have the votes before they were cast but did not have a majority when the votes were counted. ... ELVING: There's a lot of anger about this out there, especially among people who wanted the Democrats to do a lot on Day 1. The problem is they won't actually have the majority in the House until January 3, when the new Congress convenes. So Day 1 for the new majority is still seven weeks away. This week's vote on Hegseth was forced by a rogue Republican but scheduled and managed by the current Republican leadership. They got every other Republican who voted to oppose the impeachment - they are still the majority party. That's what made the difference. But there were no-shows for the vote in both parties. And in the final tally, it appeared that, had all the Democrats gotten there, they could have prevailed. And that, of course, assumes that the current GOP leadership would allow the vote to end that way when they had more Republican votes available, as well. So how much difference did this vote make? Hegseth will still face investigations and impeachment when the Democrats actually do take over, and then the Senate will need two-thirds to convict and remove him. The Senate is more likely to do that in January with its new Democratic majority than it would have been with its current majority right now.

items.excerpt: - Nov 14, 2026 - Nov 14, 2026 Updated 20 mins ago Trailblazing film producers Christine Vachon and Pamela Koffler make Governors Awards history Christine Vachon and Pamela Koffler, co-founders of Killer Films, are making history Sunday with their honorary Oscar at the Governors Awards. They are the first female producing team and independent producers to receive the Irving G. Thalberg Memorial Award. Known for bold, independent films like “Boys Don’t Cry” and “Safe,” they have produced over 100 films. Their work has been pivotal in New Queer Cinema and includes cult classics like “Hedwig and the Angry Inch.” Despite challenges, they remain optimistic and continue to create innovative films. They have a new project, “De Noche,” starring Pedro Pascal and Danny Ramirez. Rock & Roll Hall of Fame induction set for Los Angeles, with many big names skipping the stage LOS ANGELES (AP) — The Rock & Roll Hall of Fame induction ceremony on Saturday may feel like an '80s night. New members include Billy Idol, Phil Collins, Sade, Queen Latifah, New Order, Luther Vandross, and Iron Maiden. The ceremony takes place at the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles, but many inductees won’t perform or appear. The show won't be streaming live this year. An edited version airs on ABC and Disney+ on Dec. 9. Hip-hop could be the highlight with Wu-Tang Clan, Queen Latifah, and MC Lyte expected to perform. The show is in Los Angeles for the second straight year. Incoming congressman Bobby Pulido was just one political moment at the Latin Grammys Bobby Pulido is a member-elect for the U.S. House of Representatives who has also recently won the Latin Grammy for best Tejano album. He accepted the award Thursday at a ceremony in Las Vegas that reflected a broader trend of political advocacy in music. Pulido recently won a competitive race to flip Texas’ 15th Congressional District. He announced his retirement from music onstage and other artists called for unity and representation. Daddy Yankee and Anitta highlighted issues in Puerto Rico and Brazil. Political references had long been dormant from the awards. Filipino singer Carmelle storms to victory in Eurovision Asia debut in Bangkok BANGKOK (AP) — Filipino singer Carmelle won the first Asian edition of the Eurovision Song Contest with a fiery performance of “Sobra-Sobra,” beating 10 other acts in the grand final in Bangkok. Votes from national juries and viewers worldwide determined the winner. Thai duo Mang x Daou placed second with “Aroma,” followed by Vietnam’s Tóc Tiên with “Em Tiên.” Contestants arrived on tuk-tuks, waving their national flags. Bulgarian singer Dara, winner of the 70th Eurovision Song Contest, performed as a special guest. The contest seeks to put music first, though it often faces political challenges.

items.title: Entertainment news roundup: 14 November 2026 | SVCZZ
items.excerpt: ## Trailers and first looks Sony Pictures Classics has released the official US teaser trailer for Iron Boy, Louis Clichy’s hand-drawn animated feature and winner of the Special Jury Prize in Un Certain Regard at Cannes. The film opens in limited release on 4 December 2026, with a nationwide release on 22 January 2027. Keerthy Suresh plays Savithiri, a lawyer fighting to save her husband, in the trailer for Sathyavan Savithiri, out now ahead of the film’s 20 November 2026 theatrical release. Mysskin plays a major part. Bhuvan Bam is back as Titu Mama in the Dhindora season 2 trailer, with Sanjeeda Sheikh joining the cast as Kavita Mami. The new season premieres on Netflix on 20 November 2026. A young man who moves to Kathmandu to change his life after being unable to succeed in his studies is the subject of Gobar Ganesh, whose trailer is out. The Nepali film is directed by Marichman Shrestha and stars Balchhi and Barsha Siwakoti. It reaches cinemas on Magh 1. Dhiraaj Rajbanshi’s Himalayan Gold has a second trailer out, ahead of its 20 November 2026 cinema release. Sunil Thapa, Karma, Parikshya Limbu and Rahul Mukhia star. Dhanush and Mammootty share the screen for the first time in the OM: Chapter 1 trailer, out now. Rajkumar Periasamy directs, and the film opens in theatres worldwide on 20 November 2026. Christopher Briney and Michelle Randolph star in Clashing Through the Snow, whose first trailer is out. The holiday road-trip romantic comedy, directed by Carlson Young, premieres on Prime Video on 23 November 2026. The 1960 plot to assassinate Fidel Castro during his United Nations visit is the subject of Killing Castro, whose official trailer Lionsgate has released. Produced by Curtis “50 Cent” Jackson and DJ Khaled, it opens in cinemas on 11 December 2026 and arrives on digital on 18 December. D Gukesh, R Praggnanandhaa, R Vaishali, Arjun Erigaisi and Vidit Gujrathi are the subjects of CANDIDATES, a six-episode series whose official trailer Dopamine Media has released. It premieres on the Dopamine Media YouTube channel on 22 November 2026. ## Casting and production Cristiano Ronaldo has begun production on Day 1s, his first television show. The scripted drama follows a fictional elite football agency and comes from UR-Marv, with Ronaldo executive producing and expected to make his acting debut. No platform or release date has been announced. School Spirits has confirmed its season 4 cast, with 12 stars returning and one promoted to series regular. Christian Weissmann, Katharine Isabella, Clara Alexandrova and Briana Buckmaster join as guest stars, and production is under way. Vishwambhara, Chiranjeevi’s fantasy adventure known during production as Mega 156, has begun its regular shoot. The film is directed by Vassishta and produced by UV Creations, and is billed as the costliest film of Chiranjeevi’s career. Isla Fisher and Blake Ritson have joined Al Pacino in Captivated, Dito Montiel’s thriller about the kidnapping of John Paul Getty III, with Jackson Kelly also joining the cast. Production is under way in Calabria and Rome in Italy. Apple TV has promoted Samba Schutte to series regular for Pluribus season 2. His Mr. Diabate returns with an expanded presence after two guest episodes in season 1. No premiere date has been announced. Netflix has announced Pushpak Vimaan, a crime-caper comedy series from Sudip Sharma starring Jaideep Ahlawat, Abhishek Banerjee and Barun Sobti. No premiere date was given with the announcement. Kai Cech is to voice Shanti in Lost in Mandala, the first global animated feature from Nepal’s Incessant Rain Studios. The film is directed by former Disney visual effects supervisor Kiran Bhakta Joshi, with a screenplay by Zack Stentz, and is now in pre-production with no release date announced. MobLand season 3 starts production next week. Helen Mirren confirmed the start on the A Talent for Murder red carpet, with Tom Hardy and Pierce Brosnan returning. The season 2 finale airs on 20 November 2026. Freya Allan is to lead System, a horror film from director Joachim Ronning. Filming is under way in abandoned London Underground stations and tunnels, with Denzel Baidoo and Felix Edwards co-starring. ## Box office and streaming Ramayana: Rise of a Legend has crossed $100 million worldwide in seven days, with Rs 944.55 crore reported by Sacnilk. CNBC TV18 reports it as the first film outside China to reach the mark in 2026. The Kannada dubbed version of Ramayana: Part 1 has crossed Rs 50 crore net in India, the first Bollywood film to do so. It took Rs 48.95 crore in its eight-day opening week plus Rs 1.17 crore on day 9, and the Karnataka gross across all languages has passed Rs 100 crore. Paper Tiger has debuted at 85 percent on Rotten Tomatoes from 114 reviews. The James Gray crime drama stars Adam Driver, Miles Teller and Scarlett Johansson, and opened in limited release on 13 November 2026. Hulu has set 13 January 2027 as the premiere date for The Spot, an A24 psychological thriller starring Claire Danes and Ewan McGregor as a surgeon and her schoolteacher husband who suspect she caused a child’s hit-and-run death. First-look images were released on 12 November 2026.
